articles.title: 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan welcomes LeBron James to Philly after scoring: MLS roundup
articles.summary: Teenager welcomes LeBron to 76ers. Vincent Janssen scores Timbers’ first MLS hat-trick. Embolo scores, Messi assists in charged match. Philadelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history ⁠to record a five-match goal contribution streak on Saturday.
body: At 16 years and 342 ⁠days old, ⁠Sullivan ​scored in his third consecutive MLS match on Saturday when he tallied in the ⁠75th minute of the Union’s 2-0 victory over CF Montreal. He has three goals and ⁠three assists during his past five league matches.

Sullivan’s 11 ​goal contributions (four goals, seven ‌assists) on ‌the season are the most ever by a 16-year-old in ‌MLS history, eclipsing the mark set by Freddy Adu (four goals, six assists) in 2005.
So how did Sullivan celebrate his accomplishment? Well, by mimicking the newest superstar in Philadelphia, LeBron James, with the latter’s ‌chalk toss.

“I was waiting to do that for a while,” Sullivan said of the ​celebration. “I had Kim, our photographer, holding the chalk for multiple games. I just kept missing out on it! Tonight, great crowd, I figured it was the perfect ⁠time.”

articles.title: ‘What are we doing?’: Brennan’s anger at racing in 44C heat as Van Aert wins shortened stage
articles.summary: ‘It wouldn’t surprise me if some got heatstroke’ Spain’s Enric Mas retains leader’s red jersey. Britain’s Matthew Brennan expressed his disbelief at the extreme heat riders had to endure on Sunday during stage 15 of the Vuelta a España.
body: “It’s 41 degrees average,” Brennan said. “When I was on the climb at the start it was 44, and at that point you start thinking: ‘What are we doing?’ A normal office person has to have the temperature set at 20 degrees or whatever, and I’m sure that the UCI [cycling’s governing body] office will have their 20 as well.”

The medium mountain stage from Palma del Rio to Córdoba was originally scheduled to cover 189.7km, but organisers removed 79.5km from the middle ⁠of the route after activating the extreme weather ​protocol following ​several days of severe ​heat.
Brennan said: “It’s not great, but we do it, and that’s the show we put on. But it wouldn’t surprise me if there were a few bodies coming home tonight with heatstroke.”

Van Aert claimed his second victory ⁠in three stages after winning a five-rider sprint. The Belgian rider covered ⁠every attack from his four breakaway companions in the closing kilometres before producing a late ⁠surge just before the finish line to beat Alessandro ​Romele, of XDS Astana, ‌and Lidl-Trek’s Thibau ‌Nys.

articles.title: Casey beaten on fourth play-off hole in Switzerland
articles.summary: England's Paul Casey is beaten by South Africa's defending champion Thriston Lawrence on the fourth play-off hole at the European Masters in Switzerland.
body: The tournament was played at the Crans-sur-Sierre Golf Club in Crans-Montana, and Casey had pledged to donate his entire winnings to the victims of the New Year's Eve fire that killed 40 people in the Swiss mountain resort.
The 49-year-old Englishman missed four putts for the first prize of $637,500 (£469,112) - the first on his final hole in regulation and the next three on the first three play-off holes.

But after firing his approach to the back edge of the green at the fourth play-off hole, the former Ryder Cup player missed a chip and Lawrence sank his birdie putt to win the tournament for the third time - equalling the record of Seve Ballesteros.
Casey fired a two-under-par 68 in his final round to finish level on 18 under, with Lawrence forcing a play-off thanks to a stunning 62.

articles.title: Tim Wellens pulls away on last stage to win Tour of Britain
articles.summary: Belgian beats Briton Lewis Askey into second. Bradley Wiggins’ son Ben finishes in 10th. Tim Wellens, teammate to Tadej Pogacar at the UAE Emirates XRG team, took overall victory in the men’s Tour of Britain, after the Belgian rider had decisively snatched the overall race lead on the fourth stage…
body: Wellens had started the final stage in Earlston 21 seconds ahead of Lewis Askey but extended that advantage to 42sec by the finish. The British rider finished second overall after riding impressively through the earlier stages, while Ben Wiggins, son of Sir Bradley Wiggins, placed 10th overall.

The Belgian rider’s German teammate, Nils Politt, took a rare win in the final stage on Sunday, as Pogacar’s team celebrated another well-executed overall victory after a select group, which included five of their riders, broke clear of the peloton in the Lammermuir hills.
“It was a very successful week,” Wellens said. “We came here for the GC and today we also have this stage victory, so everything’s been perfect.”

The 165-kilometre stage on Saturday from Helmsley to Leyburn was won by Cees Bol of the Netherlands, but the Tour de France stage winner Wellens did enough on the short sharp climbs of the Yorkshire Dales and North York Moors, to distance the overnight leader Askey and take what proved to be an unassailable lead.

articles.title: Antonelli ends Italy’s 60-year wait for home F1 win with Monza triumph from 19th
articles.summary: Italian overhauls George Russell late on at Monza. Verstappen third for Red Bull, with Hamilton sixth. Kimi Antonelli won the Italian Grand Prix with an extraordinary drive for Mercedes at Monza, coming back from 19th on the grid to take his first win at his home race.
body: Lewis Hamilton was sixth, while his Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc walked away unhurt from a huge accident early in the race when he went off at Parabolica.

Mercedes had hoped Antonelli, who had a grid penalty for taking a new set of engine components before the race, might do well to come back as high as fifth at best. Antonelli, as he has repeatedly this season, once more exceeded their expectations. Still only 20, the Italian has made his mark with emphatic effect and even the Ferrari fans were moved to roar their approval at the home hero, even in Mercedes kit.

Italy has not had a home victor at Monza since Ludovico Scarfiotti, 60 years ago, while only one driver has come back to win from further down the grid, John Watson from 22nd at the Long Beach GP in 1983.

Not only was it an exceptional performance but one which has moved Antonelli a significant step closer to taking the world championship. Russell, who started from second on the grid, had gone into the weekend expecting to claw some points back from his teammate’s 59-point lead but is now 66 in arrears.

articles.title: Itoje returns to England squad for training camp
articles.summary: Second row Maro Itoje returns to the England set-up after being named in a 36-man training squad for this autumn's Nations Championship matches.
body: Itoje missed matches against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina in July, taking his first proper summer break from rugby in more than a decade.
The 31-year-old, whose mother died shortly before he led England through a deflating Six Nations campaign that featured only one win, has said he has felt the benefits of his time away.
Steve Borthwick's players meet up on Sunday for the first time since their summer tour.
Saracens' Itoje is expected to reclaim the captaincy from Jamie George when England play Australia on 8 November.

articles.title: Carpenter shines in convincing Sale Prem Cup win
articles.summary: Sale (17) 50. Tries: Roebuck, Carpenter 3, Raymont, Roe, Jibulu, Longstaff Cons: Lozowski 5. Bath (14) 28. Tries: Tuipulotu, Griffin, Spandler, Carr-Smith Cons: Donoghue 4.
body: Sale Sharks got their Prem Rugby Cup campaign off to an emphatic start with a dominant performance as they beat Bath 50-28 in their opening Group A fixture at the CorpAcq Stadium.
In a clash between two previous winners of the tournament in its current format - Sale winning in 2019-20 and Bath in 2024-25 - the hosts were the ones who looked capable of adding a second.

Tom Roebuck got the Sharks off to a flier on three minutes, racing on to a Joe Carpenter kick into the corner to dab down, before Bath responded with two tries of their own to take an early 14-5 lead.

But a 16-minute hat-trick from Sale full back Carpenter, either side of the half-time break, kickstarted a run of seven unanswered tries for Sale, allowing them to regain the lead and then stretch clear.

articles.title: Arsenal edge out Chelsea in pulsating London derby
articles.summary: Arsenal came from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 in the first real major Premier League heavyweight clash of the new campaign - in an early contender for game of the season.
body: Both London rivals produced a Sunday afternoon treat which rubberstamped Arsenal's credentials as the team to beat - and Chelsea's as worthy challengers for the top honours.

A pulsating game started right from the off as Morgan Rogers - sought after by Arsenal this summer - crashed new club Chelsea ahead after just 77 seconds. That poked the bear of the champions - who produced a response.
After Riccardo Calafiori saw a goal disallowed for offside, former Blue Kai Havertz got his fourth goal against his old club for Arsenal with a strike from the edge of the box.
But despite a dominant Arsenal display, Chelsea still went inches away from a second as Rogers curled wide and Pedro Neto hit the post.

articles.title: Leclerc Fires Back at Hamilton’s Feud Claims After Violent Monza Contact
articles.summary: Sparks flew immediately between the two Ferrari drivers at the 2026 Italian Grand Prix. Before Charles Leclerc’s race ended with a massive shunt into the Parabolica barriers on Lap 2, the Monegasque driver engaged in a fierce wheel-to-wheel scrap with his teammate Lewis Hamilton through the opening…
body: Now, Leclerc is pushing back against the media frenzy, rejecting the idea of a brewing civil war inside Maranello while admitting their on-track aggression crossed the line.

The intense battle through the Variante del Rettifilo left Hamilton fuming over the radio. Following the race, leaked audio captured Hamilton expressing extreme frustration with Ferrari’s lack of internal structure, comparing the chaos to his notoriously toxic championship battles with Nico Rosberg at Mercedes. “When I was at Mercedes, we had written rules of engagement,” Hamilton stated. “Here, there are no rules. We need to address that”.
When asked by the media about the Turn 1 and Turn 2 contact, Leclerc quickly shut down the premise of a bitter, intra-team rivalry.
“Yeah, I don’t really know who is forcing that narrative that we are one against the other,” Leclerc stated. “I mean, honestly, Zandvoort, there was way too many talks already”.

articles.title: Kerjota scores dramatic added-time winner as Hearts beat Dundee
articles.summary: Sabah Kerjota scored a stoppage-time winner as Hearts staged a dramatic late fightback to defeat Dundee 2-1 at Tynecastle and make it four Premiership victories in a row.
body: Hearts were frustrated for long periods after the visitors - who had both Joe Westley and Fin Robertson stretchered off - took the lead in the 17th minute through Bradley Fink.
But Hearts eventually drew level in the 84th minute through a Claudio Braga penalty before Dundee had Zan Besir sent off as the match ticked into stoppage time.
Wouter Vrancken's buoyant side made their extra man count when Albanian substitute Kerjota drilled in his first goal since arriving at Tynecastle last summer in the sixth minute of added time.
The victory elevated the Jambos, unbeaten in eight in all competitions, to second in the table.

articles.title: Erdenali shines at top table to claim Prix du Moulin honours
articles.summary: Erdenali graduated to the highest level in impressive style when proving too strong for the raiding party in the Qatar Prix du Moulin de Longchamp.
body: A strong British and Irish contingent went to post for the Group One contest, with Aidan O'Brien's Irish 2,000 Guineas hero Gstaad the hot favourite ahead of Charlie Appleby's Opera Ballo and the Ed Walker-trained Ten Bob Tony.

Unlike that trio, Francis-Henri Graffard's Erdenali was unproven in Group One company, but he had looked an exciting prospect in winning his first three starts and was an unlucky loser when third in a Group Three on his most recent outing.

With Opera Ballo taken on for the lead by Gstaad's pacemaker Dorset, Appleby's charge was a spent force entering the final furlong, at which stage Erdenali and the shock Queen Anne winner Ten Bob Tony moved up to dispute the lead.

Erdenali was always getting the better of that particular battle, however, and the pair drew clear of Gstaad, who never threatened to land a telling blow and was ultimately a bit disappointing in third.
